headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Prefect can egress broadly while the RAG course agent handles secrets and writes files, creating unsafe default data flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented, so direct prompt injection between prefect and production-agentic-rag-course is not evidenced. However, the course agent can read/write files and run subprocesses, so if Prefect outputs are manually copied into its notebooks or stdin, injection becomes plausible. The pathway is unusual and not default.
conditions: IF Prefect outputs are manually pasted into the course agent's stdin or notebooks, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file is introduced between the two agents, the course agent may parse attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting agent outputs into prompts.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Use a strict template for any handoff text.
Review any shared file before the course agent consumes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect has broad network egress, and the course agent touches configuration secrets plus academic papers and paper metadata. Even without a documented shared filesystem, the course agent's local development environment and file access create a plausible path for sensitive content to flow into Prefect-triggered API calls or logs. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the course agent stores secrets or paper content in files that Prefect reads, those contents can be exfiltrated over network egress.
IF Prefect tasks log workflow metadata containing secrets, those logs may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any files Prefect can read.
Restrict Prefect network destinations to approved endpoints.
Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager, not project files.
Audit logs for accidental secret inclusion.
Run the agents in separate directories.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration/data-engineering agent with broad egress, while the course agent can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Their write surfaces overlap on the local environment, so concurrent modification conflicts are plausible even though shared-state locking is not documented. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF Prefect tasks and course-agent subprocesses write the same artifact, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
Use file locks for any shared path.
Make one agent read-only for the shared workspace.
Check for collisions before each run.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can orchestrate workflows, and the course agent exposes /api/v1/ask and /api/v1/agentic-ask style interfaces plus shell execution. If Prefect-produced outputs are treated as authoritative inputs, the course agent may act on them without verification. That creates a default-path cascade from one agent's output into the other's actions, but no direct evidence of automation-to-action chaining is provided.
conditions: IF Prefect output is fed into the course agent's ask or agentic-ask endpoint without validation, errors can cascade.
IF the course agent executes shell commands derived from Prefect outputs, incorrect facts can trigger bad actions.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Validate Prefect outputs against a schema.
Require source citations before downstream action.
Disable automatic execution of generated commands.
Log and diff handoff payloads.

E_compliance.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata, while the course agent handles configuration secrets and academic/paper metadata in a local development environment. The pair suggests retention and logging mismatch risk, especially if Prefect stores workflow metadata longer than the course agent expects. No residency or regulated-data claim is documented, so this is a compliance-gap medium rather than high.
conditions: IF workflow metadata from the course agent is retained by Prefect longer than the course agent's local policy, a retention mismatch exists.
IF secrets are written into workflow metadata, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Set explicit retention limits for workflow metadata.
Exclude secrets from logs and traces.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
Purge old runs after validation.
Keep regulated data out of the shared workflow.
